hepatic.value: No dose adjustment is required in patients with mild hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh class A). Because patients with moderate hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh class B) may have intrinsic coagulation abnormalities and there is limited clinical experience with ELIQUIS in these patients, dosing recommendations cannot be provided. ELIQUIS is not recommended in patients with severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh class C).

value: PREMATURE DISCONTINUATION OF ELIQUIS INCREASES THE RISK OF THROMBOTIC EVENTS: Premature discontinuation of any oral anticoagulant, including ELIQUIS, increases the risk of thrombotic events. If anticoagulation with ELIQUIS is discontinued for a reason other than pathological bleeding or completion of a course of therapy, consider coverage with another anticoagulant.

SPINAL/EPIDURAL HEMATOMA: Epidural or spinal hematomas may occur in patients treated with ELIQUIS who are receiving neuraxial anesthesia or undergoing spinal puncture. These hematomas may result in long-term or permanent paralysis.

mechanism_of_action.value: Apixaban is a selective inhibitor of FXa. It does not require antithrombin III for antithrombotic activity. Apixaban inhibits free and clot-bound FXa, and prothrombinase activity. Apixaban has no direct effect on platelet aggregation, but indirectly inhibits platelet aggregation induced by thrombin.

refs.quote: Apixaban is a selective inhibitor of FXa. It does not require antithrombin III for antithrombotic activity. Apixaban inhibits free and clot-bound FXa, and prothrombinase activity. Apixaban has no direct effect on platelet aggregation, but indirectly inhibits platelet aggregation induced by thrombin.

Apixaban is a substrate of both CYP3A4 and P-gp. Inhibitors of CYP3A4 and P-gp increase exposure to apixaban and increase the risk of bleeding. Inducers of CYP3A4 and P-gp decrease exposure to apixaban and increase the risk of stroke and other thromboembolic events.

missed_dose.value: If a dose of ELIQUIS is not taken at the scheduled time, the dose should be taken as soon as possible on the same day and twice-daily administration should be resumed. The dose should not be doubled to make up for a missed dose.

value.drug_or_class: Combined P-gp and Strong CYP3A4 Inhibitors (Ketoconazole, Itraconazole, Ritonavir)
value.effect: Dual inhibition of P-gp and CYP3A4 significantly increases apixaban exposure, doubling AUC and increasing the risk of major bleeding.
value.management: Reduce ELIQUIS dose by 50% for patients taking 5 mg or 10 mg twice daily. If already taking 2.5 mg twice daily, avoid coadministration.

refs.locator: Section 7.1 Combined P-gp and Strong CYP3A4 Inhibitors
refs.quote: For patients receiving ELIQUIS 5 mg or 10 mg twice daily, the dose of ELIQUIS should be decreased by 50% when coadministered with drugs that are combined P-gp and strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g., ketoconazole, itraconazole, ritonavir)

value.drug_or_class: Combined P-gp and Strong CYP3A4 Inducers (Rifampin, St. John's Wort)
value.effect: Strong induction decreases apixaban AUC by ~50%, markedly increasing the risk of ischemic stroke and systemic thromboembolism.
value.management: Avoid concomitant use of apixaban with combined P-gp and strong CYP3A4 inducers.

refs.locator: Section 7.2 Combined P-gp and Strong CYP3A4 Inducers
refs.quote: Avoid concomitant use of ELIQUIS with combined P-gp and strong CYP3A4 inducers (e.g., rifampin, carbamazepine, phenytoin, St. John’s wort) because such drugs will decrease exposure to apixaban

value.effect: Additive impairment of hemostasis substantially increases the risk of clinically overt and major gastrointestinal/intracranial bleeding.
value.management: Co-administer only when clinically indicated (e.g. acute ACS / post-PCI) with cautious monitoring of bleeding signs and symptoms.
